background: I have worked on 29 projects and hold 22 certifications across backend development and related fields. You can see examples of past work on my Resume page and view my full list of certifications on the Certifications page.
whyWorkWithMe: I have spent 6+ years focused mainly on backend engineering. I am not someone who touches the backend now and then. I think about data, structure and growth first. I write code that is easy for someone else, or future me, to pick up later. I work across Laravel, WordPress and Strapi depending on what each project actually needs, instead of forcing every project into the same tool.

faq.q: What services do you offer?
faq.a: I offer custom software solutions, Laravel and PHP development, WordPress development, Strapi based web app development, web security audits and hardening, API development and integration, migration and modernization, backend performance optimization, and ongoing maintenance and support. This covers tailored business software, custom backend systems, APIs, admin panels, plugins, themes, content infrastructure, security, performance and long term upkeep.

faq.q: How do I choose the right service for my project?
faq.a: If you need a system built around a specific business process that does not fit existing tools, custom software solutions is usually the right fit. If you need a custom application or API built from scratch, Laravel and PHP is a strong choice. If you already use WordPress or want a content heavy site, WordPress development is a good match. If you need structured content delivered to more than one place, or a content powered application, Strapi based development is the right fit. If you are connecting existing tools or need a solid API layer, API development and integration covers that. If you are worried about security, or need to meet a security requirement, a security audit and hardening is the right starting point. If your system is old and getting harder to maintain, migration and modernization is worth considering. If the site is slow and growing slower, start with backend performance optimization. And if you already have a system you want to keep healthy, ongoing maintenance and support keeps it that way. If you are not sure, reach out and I can help you decide.

faq.q: Do you work with businesses outside Pakistan?
faq.a: Yes. I work remotely with clients in different countries and time zones.

faq.q: How long does a typical project take?
faq.a: This depends on the size and scope of the project. A small plugin or feature may take a couple of weeks. A full application or CMS setup can take a few months. I can give a clear timeline once I understand the project.

cta: Not sure which service fits your project? Let us talk about it.

services.title: Custom Software Solutions
services.metaDescription: Custom software and tailored web application development for business tools, portals, multi-tenant platforms and systems engineered around your exact workflows.
services.hero: Software built around your actual needs, not a template. Systems designed for the way your business works, not the other way around.
services.overview: Not every business problem fits neatly into an off-the-shelf product. Custom software is for the parts of your business that need to work the way you do. I take the time to understand how your team actually operates, then build a system that fits that workflow. This could be a tool that replaces a messy spreadsheet process, a portal that connects customers to your services, or a platform that automates a repetitive part of your operation. Whatever the problem, the goal is the same. Software that does the job well today and is easy to change as your business grows.
whatIBuild: Business tools and portals built around your exact workflow
Web applications that replace manual or spreadsheet based processes
Member, client and customer management systems
Automation that removes repetitive manual work
Integration between the tools your business already uses
Systems built on PHP, Laravel or WordPress, whichever fits best
services.howIWork: I start with the problem, not the technology. We talk through how your business works today, where the friction is, and what you want the end result to feel like. Only then do I decide on the stack. I build in stages and keep you in the loop, so there are no surprises at the end. When it is live, you get software that fits how your team works, with room to grow.
services.whyItMatters: Off-the-shelf tools make you adapt to them. Custom software adapts to you. That means fewer workarounds, less manual data entry, and a system your team actually wants to use. Because it is built around your process from day one, it is also cheaper to maintain and easier to extend later than forcing a generic product to fit.

faq.q: When does custom software make sense?
faq.a: When an existing tool almost works but not quite, or when your team is spending too much time on manual workarounds. If the cost of those workarounds keeps growing, a tailored system usually pays for itself.

faq.q: Can you work around the tools we already use?
faq.a: Yes. I often build systems that connect to existing software instead of replacing it, so your team does not have to learn everything from scratch.

faq.q: How do you decide which technology to build with?
faq.a: I pick based on the problem. Laravel for solid application backends, WordPress for content heavy builds, or a custom headless CMS when that is the right fit. The decision follows the project, not the other way around.

faq.q: What if my needs change after launch?
faq.a: That is expected. Custom software is built to change. Because it is written around your process, adding new features or adjusting existing ones is straightforward rather than a fight with the tool.

services.cta: Have a process that needs its own software? Let us talk.

services.title: Custom Laravel & PHP Development
services.metaDescription: Custom Laravel API development and PHP backend engineering. Scalable REST APIs, admin panels and application architecture built to handle real traffic without breaking.
services.hero: I build backend systems that keep working once real users show up. Clean structure, fast queries and code that does not fall apart six months later.
services.overview: PHP and Laravel have been the core of my work for more than 6 years. I use them to build custom APIs, admin panels and full application backends. These are the kinds of systems that need to stay fast and stable as traffic and complexity grow. I do not like putting together something that works today and breaks under load next month. I think through the structure first. How data moves, where slow points will show up, and what happens once this system is actually being used by real people.

headings.whyItMatters: Why a Solid Laravel Backend Matters

whatIBuild: Custom Laravel applications built from the ground up
REST APIs for web, mobile and other third party tools
Admin panels and internal tools for teams
Database design and query tuning using MySQL
Caching with Redis to keep things fast at scale
Updating and rebuilding older PHP codebases
Connecting third party services and payment tools
services.howIWork: I start by understanding what the application actually needs to do. Not just a list of features, but how it will be used and where it needs to grow. From there I plan the database and the API structure before writing any application code. This means the foundation is solid and easy to build on later. I also test each part as I build it, instead of waiting until the end to see if everything fits together.
services.whyItMatters: Many backend problems do not show up right away. Slow queries under real data, code that is hard to extend, systems that were never built for the traffic they eventually get. I plan for these problems from day one so you are not paying to fix them later. A well built backend also makes it easier and cheaper to add new features down the road.

faq.q: Why should I choose Laravel over other PHP frameworks?
faq.a: Laravel comes with a lot of built in tools for common tasks like authentication, routing and database work. This means less time spent building basic pieces from scratch and more time spent on what makes your application different.

faq.q: Can you work with an existing Laravel or PHP project?
faq.a: Yes. I often step into projects that already exist, whether that means adding new features, fixing performance problems or cleaning up older code.

faq.q: Do you build both the API and the admin panel?
faq.a: Yes. I can build the full backend, including the API that powers your app or website and the admin panel your team uses to manage it.

faq.q: What if my current PHP code is old and hard to maintain?
faq.a: I can review the code, plan a path to update it safely, and rebuild the parts that need the most work without breaking what already works for your users.

services.cta: Have a Laravel or PHP project in mind? Let us talk.

services.title: Custom WordPress Plugin Development
services.metaDescription: Custom WordPress plugin development, themes and performance optimization. Clean, maintainable sites and plugins for teams that need more than a page builder can offer.
services.hero: Custom plugins, clean builds and WordPress sites that do not slow down or break as your content and traffic grow.
services.overview: I build WordPress sites and plugins the same way I build everything else. Speed and long term upkeep come first, not as an afterthought. This could mean a custom plugin built for one specific business need, a theme built from scratch, or fixing up a site that has grown past what a page builder can handle. My focus is always on making sure the site stays reliable as it grows.
whatIBuild: Custom WordPress plugins built for specific business needs
Custom themes built for speed, not just looks
API connections linking WordPress to other systems
Moving sites away from page builders to clean, custom code
Speed improvements for busy, high traffic WordPress sites
Ongoing support and maintenance
services.howIWork: Most WordPress problems come from using the wrong tool for the job. A stack of five plugins doing the work of one, or a theme that fights you every time you try to change something. I start by figuring out what the site actually needs. Sometimes that means one small custom plugin instead of five bloated ones. Sometimes it means a full custom theme built around your content and your users.
services.whyItMatters: A slow, cluttered WordPress site costs you visitors and, over time, money. I build sites that load fast because they are built lean, and that stay easy to manage because they were planned that way from day one. This also makes future updates simpler and cheaper.

faq.q: Do you build custom themes or use existing ones?
faq.a: Both, depending on your goals. If you need something unique to your brand and content, a custom theme is usually the better choice. If a solid existing theme fits your needs, I can adjust and extend it instead.

faq.q: Can you fix a slow WordPress site?
faq.a: Yes. I look at what is slowing the site down, whether that is plugins, hosting, images or the theme itself, and fix the parts that matter most.

faq.q: Do you build custom plugins for specific business needs?
faq.a: Yes. If your business has a process that does not fit into an existing plugin, I can build one that matches exactly what you need.

faq.q: Will my WordPress site be easy for my team to manage after launch?
faq.a: Yes. I build with your team in mind, so content updates and everyday changes do not require a developer every time.

services.cta: Need a WordPress build that can actually grow with you? Let us talk.

services.title: Strapi Headless CMS Development
services.metaDescription: Headless CMS development with Strapi and Next.js integration. Structured content, fast content APIs and a backend your team can actually manage.
services.hero: Content powered applications built on Strapi. A clean backend your team controls, delivered through a fast API to any frontend.
services.overview: Strapi is a headless CMS, which means content lives in a structured backend and gets delivered through an API instead of being tied to a website template. I build Strapi backends that give your team a simple dashboard to manage content, while the frontend stays fast, flexible and fully under your control. This works well for sites and applications that need the same content in more than one place, like a website and a mobile app, or that need to scale without being locked into one template system.

headings.howIWork: How I Build Headless CMS Backends

whatIBuild: Strapi content models and backend structure designed for your content
REST and GraphQL APIs that deliver content to web and mobile
Custom Strapi plugins and field types for specific business needs
Admin panel configuration that keeps content editing simple for your team
Connecting Strapi to Laravel, WordPress or any frontend
Migrating content from WordPress or other CMSes into Strapi
Performance and security hardening for production Strapi setups
services.howIWork: I start by mapping out what content your business manages and how it needs to be structured. Then I build the Strapi backend around that structure, so your team gets an admin panel that matches how they actually work. From there I wire up the API and the frontend, whether that is a Laravel app, WordPress or a modern JavaScript frontend, and make sure content edits flow through without friction.
services.whyItMatters: A headless CMS keeps your content in one place and your frontend free to change. That means your team can update content without touching code, and you are never locked into a single template or platform. Because content is delivered through a fast, structured API, sites and apps stay quick, scale cleanly and are easier to extend as your needs grow.

faq.q: What is a headless CMS and why would I use Strapi?
faq.a: A headless CMS separates content management from the frontend. Strapi stores your content and serves it through an API, so you can use that same content on a website, a mobile app or anywhere else. You get a clean admin panel for your team and total freedom over the frontend.

faq.q: Can Strapi replace my existing WordPress site?
faq.a: It depends on what you need. If you want a content heavy site where editors control everything, WordPress may still be the right fit. If you want structured content served to multiple frontends, or content that powers an application, Strapi is usually the stronger choice.

faq.q: Which frontend do you use with Strapi?
faq.a: I can connect Strapi to Laravel, WordPress or a modern JavaScript frontend. I pick based on what fits your project, since the headless setup means the frontend can be anything that consumes an API.

faq.q: Is Strapi content easy for my team to manage?
faq.a: Yes. I configure the Strapi admin panel around your content and your team's workflow, so editors manage content in a clear dashboard without needing a developer.

services.cta: Want content that works across your site and apps? Let us talk.

services.title: Web Security Audit & Hardening
services.metaDescription: OWASP compliant web development audits and hardening for Laravel, WordPress and Strapi. OWASP Top 10 checks, SQLi, XSS and CSRF reviews, and fixes backed by security certifications.
services.hero: Web application security reviews that find the real problems and fix them. Audits and hardening backed by web security and penetration testing certifications.
services.overview: Most security issues are not exotic. They are missed login checks, unchecked inputs, exposed admin panels and outdated dependencies. I review your Laravel, WordPress or Strapi application against the OWASP Top 10 and beyond, then fix what I find. This covers both a one-off audit and the hardening work that follows. I look at how your application handles authentication, authorization, input validation, file uploads and third party plugins, because those are where most real-world breaches start.

headings.howIWork: How I Approach a Security Audit

whatIBuild: Security audits covering the OWASP Top 10 and common misconfigurations
Review of authentication, authorization and session handling
Input validation, SQL injection and XSS checks
Hardening of server, framework and CMS settings
Securing admin panels and restricting exposed areas
Reviewing third party plugins, packages and dependencies for known issues
Clear reports of what was found, how serious it is, and how it was fixed
services.howIWork: I start with a review of your application, its configuration and its dependencies. Then I go through the code and running system looking for the weaknesses that matter, prioritizing by risk so you know what to fix first. I fix what I can directly and give you a clear report for anything that needs your decision. When the work is done you get a hardened system plus a checklist you can reuse after future changes.
services.whyItMatters: A security breach is expensive in ways that go beyond the fix. Stolen data, downtime and lost trust are hard to recover from. Most successful attacks exploit basic gaps that a proper review catches early. Given that I hold certifications in web application security, penetration testing and related fields, this is a service backed by training, not just experience.

faq.q: What does a security audit cover?
faq.a: I review authentication, authorization, input handling, file uploads, server and framework configuration, third party plugins and dependencies, and exposure of sensitive areas like admin panels. Findings are prioritized by risk.

faq.q: Do you only audit, or do you fix too?
faq.a: Both. I fix what I can during the engagement and provide a clear report for anything that needs your input, like decisions about how authentication should work.

faq.q: Which platforms do you audit?
faq.a: Laravel and PHP applications, WordPress sites, and Strapi setups. That covers the stacks I work with, so I review the code and the CMS ecosystem, not just the surface.

faq.q: Is this a penetration test?
faq.a: It is a security review and hardening service informed by penetration testing experience. If you need a formal pentest engagement with a specific scope and report format, we can discuss how deep that should go.

services.cta: Not sure how secure your application really is? Let us find out.

services.title: Custom REST & GraphQL API Development
services.metaDescription: Custom REST API development, GraphQL APIs and third party integrations. Payment gateways, webhooks, CRMs and tools connected to your Laravel, WordPress or Strapi system.
services.hero: APIs that work cleanly and integrations that actually connect. REST and GraphQL APIs built properly, and third party tools wired into your system.
services.overview: Modern applications run on connections. Your site talks to a payment provider, your CRM talks to your admin panel, your mobile app talks to your backend. I build the APIs that make these connections clean and reliable, and I integrate the third party services your business depends on. This covers custom REST and GraphQL APIs, payment gateways, webhooks, and connecting CRMs and other tools to Laravel, WordPress or Strapi. The focus is on APIs that are well documented, consistent and safe to build on.
whatIBuild: Custom REST APIs for web, mobile and external tools
GraphQL APIs when a flexible query interface fits better
Payment gateway and billing integrations
Webhooks to push events to your systems in real time
Connecting CRMs, email, analytics and other third party tools
API authentication, rate limiting and versioning done properly
Documentation so your team and other developers can actually use it
services.howIWork: I start by defining what the API needs to do and who will use it. That shapes the endpoints, the data shape and how authentication works. Then I build it with versioning and error handling from the start, so later changes do not break existing consumers. For integrations, I map how data should flow between the tools before writing any code, so the connection is reliable rather than fragile.
services.whyItMatters: A messy API is expensive. Every consumer built against it has to work around its problems, and every integration you add later becomes harder. A well designed API and clean integrations mean new features, new tools and new partners connect without rework, which saves real time and money as your product grows.

faq.q: Do you build APIs for existing systems or only new ones?
faq.a: Both. I can build an API layer on top of an existing Laravel, WordPress or Strapi system, or design one from scratch for a new product.

faq.q: Which payment providers can you integrate?
faq.a: I have experience with the common payment gateways used in web applications. Tell me the provider and region and I will confirm the details before quoting.

faq.q: What does API documentation include?
faq.a: Endpoints, request and response examples, authentication details and error handling. Clear enough that another developer can integrate without asking you questions.

faq.q: Can you integrate multiple tools together?
faq.a: Yes. Connecting several systems, like your site, CRM and analytics, is often where the real value is. I map the data flow so everything stays consistent.

services.cta: Have systems that need to talk to each other? Let us connect them.

services.title: Migration & Modernization
services.metaDescription: Legacy codebase modernization and PHP 8+ upgrades. Safe migration of legacy PHP, older Laravel versions and WordPress sites into modern, maintainable systems including Strapi.
services.hero: Old systems upgraded without breaking what works. Legacy PHP to Laravel, WordPress to Strapi, and everything in between, moved safely.
services.overview: Every business eventually outgrows its software. The code that worked five years ago is now slow, hard to change and risky to update. I help move systems to something modern without losing the data or breaking what users rely on. This includes migrating legacy PHP codebases to Laravel, upgrading older Laravel versions, and moving WordPress content into Strapi for a headless setup. The key is a staged plan. Nothing changes until the replacement is ready, and everything is verified along the way.

headings.howIWork: How I Plan a Safe Migration

whatIBuild: Legacy PHP codebases rebuilt on modern Laravel
Laravel version upgrades done safely, one step at a time
WordPress content and media migrated to Strapi
WordPress sites moved to cleaner custom code
Data migration with integrity checks, so nothing is lost
Feature parity checks so the new system does everything the old one did
A cutover plan that minimizes downtime and risk
services.howIWork: I start by mapping what the current system does, what data it holds and what would break if anything changed. Then I plan the migration in stages, building the new system alongside the old one rather than replacing it blind. I verify data and behavior at each stage, and only cut over when the new system is proven. This is slower than a rewrite, and it is also far safer.
services.whyItMatters: Most failed migrations happen because someone tried to move everything at once or skipped verification. A staged migration keeps your business running while the new system is built and tested. The result is a modern, maintainable codebase that you can actually extend, without the risk and downtime of a big bang rewrite.

faq.q: Is migration safer than a full rewrite?
faq.a: Usually yes. A staged migration builds the new system alongside the old one and verifies each step, so your business keeps running and nothing is lost. A rewrite from scratch carries more risk and often takes longer.

faq.q: Can you migrate my WordPress site to Strapi?
faq.a: Yes. That includes moving content, media and structure into Strapi, and connecting a frontend if you need one. WordPress and Strapi store content differently, so part of the work is mapping the structure correctly.

faq.q: Will my users see downtime during the move?
faq.a: The goal is minimal or no downtime. I build and test the new system before cutover and plan the switch so disruption to your users is as small as possible.

faq.q: How long does a migration take?
faq.a: It depends on the size of the system and how different the target is. I give a clear timeline after assessing what needs to move and what the risks are.

services.cta: Stuck on software that is getting harder to maintain? Let us plan the move.

services.title: Backend Performance Optimization
services.metaDescription: Backend performance optimization for Laravel, WordPress and Strapi. MySQL query optimization, Redis caching and database tuning with measured before and after results.
services.hero: Backends that stay fast under real traffic. Slow queries found, caching added and measured results instead of guesses.
services.overview: Performance problems are usually caused by a handful of specific things. Slow database queries, missing caching, unnecessary work on every request. I find those things instead of guessing, fix them, and measure the difference. This covers Laravel, WordPress and Strapi applications. The work includes query analysis and database tuning with MySQL, adding Redis caching where it actually helps, profiling application code and removing the repeated work that slows everything down.
whatIBuild: Database query analysis and index tuning with MySQL
Redis caching added where it actually helps, not everywhere
Application profiling to find the real bottlenecks
Removing repeated work and N+1 query patterns
Response time measurement before and after, so you see the gain
Loading and traffic handling improvements for real usage patterns
services.howIWork: I do not optimize by guesswork. I start by measuring, with query logs, profiling and response time checks, to find what is actually slow. Then I fix the highest impact issues first and measure again. You get a before and after picture, so the improvement is visible rather than assumed. I also leave your codebase clean enough that future work does not undo the gains.
services.whyItMatters: Slow sites cost visitors and revenue, and the cost usually grows as data and traffic do. The same fixes that bring a slow page from seconds to milliseconds also make the system cheaper to run, because they reduce the server resources every request burns. Optimizing the real bottlenecks is cheaper than scaling up hardware to cover for them.

faq.q: Can you speed up an existing application without breaking it?
faq.a: Yes. I work from measurements, fix the highest impact bottlenecks and verify behavior stays correct at each step. Optimization that changes how the app behaves is not optimization, so I avoid it.

faq.q: How do you know what is actually slow?
faq.a: I measure. Query logs, application profiling and response time checks show where the time is really going, instead of relying on assumptions about what is slow.

faq.q: Do you work on WordPress performance too?
faq.a: Yes. WordPress slowdowns usually come from plugins, queries or configuration, and I review those areas the same way I would a Laravel or Strapi application.

faq.q: Will I see measured results?
faq.a: Yes. I compare response times and query performance before and after, so you see the actual improvement rather than a general promise.

services.cta: Site getting slower as it grows? Let us find out why.

services.title: Ongoing Maintenance & Support

services.hero: Ongoing care for the systems you rely on. Security updates, bug fixes and monitoring handled, so you are not left holding it alone after launch.
services.overview: Launch day is not the end of the work. Software needs updates, monitoring, and fixing when things break. I offer maintenance and support retainers for Laravel, WordPress and Strapi systems, covering security updates for frameworks and dependencies, bug fixes, small changes, and keeping an eye on uptime and health. You get a developer who already knows your system, instead of explaining it to someone new every time something goes wrong.
whatIBuild: Regular security updates for frameworks, dependencies and plugins
Bug fixing and small changes as they come up
Uptime and health monitoring with clear alerts
Backup checks so recovery is possible when you need it
Documentation of your system so issues are resolved faster
A predictable monthly cost instead of emergency pricing
services.howIWork: I start by getting to know your system, its setup and its known weak points, so I am not reading about it for the first time when something breaks. Then we agree on a level of support, from keeping dependencies updated to a fuller package with monitoring and small changes. Issues get handled promptly, and anything urgent gets prioritized the way it should.
services.whyItMatters: Unmaintained software is a risk. Outdated dependencies are how most sites get compromised, and an unmonitored system can be down for hours before anyone notices. A maintenance retainer turns that around. You get someone who already knows your code, regular updates that close the gaps, and support you can rely on at a predictable cost.

faq.q: What does a maintenance retainer include?
faq.a: Security updates, bug fixes, monitoring and small changes, depending on the package. We agree on scope up front so you know what is covered and what is a separate request.

faq.q: How fast will you respond to urgent issues?
faq.a: Urgent issues get priority treatment. Exact response times depend on the package, and we agree on those before you commit.

faq.q: Do you maintain systems you did not build?
faq.a: Yes. I can take over support for existing Laravel, WordPress or Strapi systems, starting with a review so I understand how it is built and where the risks are.

faq.q: Can I get maintenance only when I need it?
faq.a: Yes. Alongside regular retainers I can handle one-off fixes, updates or audits on request, with a clear quote before any work starts.

services.cta: Do not carry your system alone. Let us talk about support.
